offerings.audience: Evaluation engineers and reviewer-operations teams.
offerings.job: Validate rubrics, score approved fixtures, audit reviewer agreement and leakage, and generate portable evaluation reports.
offerings.differentiator: One local Python CLI keeps rubric checks, deterministic scoring, reviewer QA, leakage checks, and evidence reports in the same inspectable workflow.
offerings.proof: Validated rubric output, score records, agreement and leakage findings, plus self-contained HTML and Markdown reports.
offerings.boundary: Inputs and reports remain local or inside the operator's CI environment unless the operator uploads them elsewhere.
offerings.nextAction: Run the packaged examples, inspect the generated report, and verify the installed version against PyPI and the source tag.

offerings.audience: Python engineers integrating hosted AuraOne workflows.
offerings.job: Call hosted evaluation, analytics, training-export, and governance APIs from Python services, notebooks, and automation.
offerings.differentiator: Typed sync and async clients share an explicit credential, base-URL, output, error, and retry contract.
offerings.proof: Typed client methods, deterministic CLI output modes, stable exit codes, clean-package tests, and registry provenance evidence.
offerings.boundary: Only explicit API requests are sent to the configured AuraOne base URL; credentials remain in the operator's environment.
offerings.nextAction: Install in a clean environment, run a read-only command with JSON output, and compare the package version and hashes with PyPI.

offerings.audience: TypeScript and Node.js application and platform engineers.
offerings.job: Integrate hosted AuraOne evaluation workflows through typed REST and GraphQL clients.
offerings.differentiator: The package makes runtime targets, exports, retries, polling, credential handling, and response types inspectable from one public contract.
offerings.proof: Generated declarations, package exports, clean-consumer tests, packed tarball inspection, and npm provenance evidence.
offerings.boundary: Requests go only to the configured AuraOne API; browser credentials must be scoped and protected by the host application.
offerings.nextAction: Install in a clean Node.js project, compile one typed request, and verify the tarball and source tag shown by npm.

offerings.audience: Repository owners who gate pull requests with evaluation evidence.
offerings.job: Run AuraOne evaluations for an exact commit and publish one lifecycle-aware Check Run plus one idempotent evidence summary.
offerings.differentiator: Check state, evaluated commit, threshold, template evidence, remediation, permissions, and deployment identity remain attached to one native review path.
offerings.proof: GitHub Check Run output, bot-owned summary marker, webhook tests, package contents, and deployed-app permission evidence.
offerings.boundary: The self-hosted app reads configured repository context, calls AuraOne, and writes only the approved Checks and optional summary comment.
offerings.nextAction: Review the required permissions and webhook events, test against a non-production repository, and verify package and deployed revision identity.

offerings.audience: Maintainers of Rubric, Agent, and Robotics Studio Open.
offerings.job: Provide the shared shell, contracts, release controls, keychain bridge, updater conventions, and evidence infrastructure for the three desktop Studios.
offerings.differentiator: Shared runtime and release behavior is implemented once while each product keeps its own workflow and visual hierarchy.
offerings.proof: Platform contract tests, distribution manifests, security gates, release-evidence schemas, and clean package builds.
offerings.boundary: The platform is source infrastructure; product-specific data movement depends on the consuming Studio and its configured adapters.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect the shared contracts and distribution evidence before consuming a package or building a flagship binary.

offerings.audience: Open-source maintainers building evidence-heavy technical interfaces.
offerings.job: Provide OSS-safe semantic tokens and evidence UI primitives without shipping AuraOne's private font binaries.
offerings.differentiator: The package separates public token and component contracts from the private official-font delivery boundary.
offerings.proof: Token CSS, component tests, accessibility checks, public-asset verification, and package-content inspection.
offerings.boundary: No private font binary is included; consuming public apps use declared fallbacks unless an authorized same-origin font boundary is available.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect the packed files and token contract, then verify the exact npm version before adding it to a public application.

offerings.audience: Maintainers of dense local-first developer workbenches.
offerings.job: Provide tested shell, navigation, telemetry, evidence, and workbench primitives for the Open Studio flagships.
offerings.differentiator: The kit is optimized for repeated technical work and inherits the shared Proofline semantic contract instead of legacy glass styling.
offerings.proof: Component tests, zero-violation accessibility audits, generated declarations, canonical CSS, and clean build output.
offerings.boundary: The package renders UI only; runtime, storage, network, and secret behavior are supplied by the consuming application.
offerings.nextAction: Review the component and style exports and verify the package is released from the same platform source train as the consuming Studio.

offerings.audience: Desktop and web engineers integrating shared Studio runtime behavior.
offerings.job: Define portable contracts for keychain access, intake signing, telemetry, updater evidence, and release boundaries.
offerings.differentiator: Applications share typed behavior while native implementations remain replaceable and fail closed.
offerings.proof: Type declarations, contract tests, native integration tests, and release-evidence validation.
offerings.boundary: The package defines interfaces and normalization; no secret or telemetry payload is sent by the package itself.
offerings.nextAction: Read the keychain and telemetry contracts, run their tests, and verify the package version matches the consuming Studio release train.

offerings.audience: Evaluation, model, and Human Data teams.
offerings.job: Author, validate, preview, calibrate, diff, and export criterion-level AI evaluation rubrics.
offerings.differentiator: Criterion definition, response samples, scoring evidence, calibration, and score-impact diff stay in one local-first decision workspace.
offerings.proof: Versioned rubric files, deterministic preview traces, calibration records, score-impact diffs, and export manifests.
offerings.boundary: Projects stay on the device unless the operator explicitly exports, shares, or connects a hosted service.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect the source and selected scoring-workspace capture; use the final DMG only after checksum, offline launch, signing, and notarization evidence is current.

offerings.audience: MCP, A2A, and agent-reliability engineers.
offerings.job: Connect agent systems, inspect tool traces, replay failures, compare candidates, and export regression evidence.
offerings.differentiator: Connection identity, tool sequence, timing, cost, payload, replay, model comparison, and release evidence remain attached to the selected trace.
offerings.proof: Portable trace cards, deterministic replay fixtures, behavior comparisons, CI exports, and native keychain-backed signing.
offerings.boundary: Trace and replay files stay local by default; network movement follows only the model, tool, endpoint, or telemetry connection configured by the operator.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect the final trace-workbench capture and runtime boundaries; use the final DMG only after offline, checksum, architecture, and signing verification.

offerings.audience: Agent engineers automating trace ingest, replay, comparison, and CI export.
offerings.job: Run Agent Studio's trace and regression workflows in terminals and CI without the visual workbench.
offerings.differentiator: CLI output and exported evidence follow the same trace, replay, and release contracts as the desktop application.
offerings.proof: Structured trace output, replay diffs, JUnit and regression artifacts, package tests, and clean-install evidence.
offerings.boundary: Local files remain local; network access occurs only through explicitly configured endpoints or providers.
offerings.nextAction: Run the synthetic trace example with machine-readable output and verify the package version and exported files before CI adoption.

offerings.audience: Robotics and embodied-AI dataset teams.
offerings.job: Synchronize robot episodes, inspect failures and recoveries, record review decisions, and export checksummed evidence.
offerings.differentiator: A dominant deterministic sensor scene, transport timeline, data health, annotations, and release decision stay synchronized in one cockpit.
offerings.proof: Synthetic fixture provenance, episode annotations, quality findings, decision records, local export archives, and capture evidence.
offerings.boundary: Review is local-first; upload or hosted movement occurs only through an explicitly configured destination adapter.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect the synchronized-episode capture and synthetic provenance; use the final DMG only after offline, checksum, architecture, and signing verification.

offerings.audience: Evaluation engineers testing a rubric and response set before installing a CLI.
offerings.job: Import rubric JSON and response JSONL, validate them, run deterministic scoring, and inspect exact evidence in the browser.
offerings.differentiator: The primary workflow runs in-browser with a Pyodide-compatible local execution boundary and shareable state instead of requiring an account.
offerings.proof: Validation output, score evidence, permalink state, deterministic fixtures, and browser interaction tests.
offerings.boundary: Imported evaluation data remains in the browser unless the user explicitly exports or shares it.
offerings.nextAction: Inspect source and run the local browser build; treat any hosted URL as current only when deployment evidence matches the source revision.

offerings.audience: Robotics reviewers who need a portable metadata-only review artifact.
offerings.job: Review event streams, failures, and decisions in one self-contained offline HTML artifact.
offerings.differentiator: The canonical viewer exports review metadata without exporting observations, actions, sensor payloads, media, or training shards.
offerings.proof: Self-contained HTML, event and decision records, metadata-only export tests, and network-independence checks.
offerings.boundary: The viewer runs offline and exports review metadata only.
offerings.nextAction: Open the generated artifact offline, verify the checksum and metadata-only export, and use an immutable release URL only after it is evidenced.

offerings.audience: Agent, robotics, and evaluation teams building regression libraries.
offerings.job: Browse, filter, validate, and reproduce public synthetic failure cases.
offerings.differentiator: Each case keeps the symptom, reproduction, expected behavior, observed behavior, tags, and contribution provenance together.
offerings.proof: Validated case records, searchable static gallery, reproduction metadata, and deterministic generated output.
offerings.boundary: Only checked-in public or approved cases are displayed; private datasets are not uploaded to the gallery.
offerings.nextAction: Run the local gallery against its synthetic cases and verify both package and hosted-static evidence before linking it as current.

offerings.audience: Repository owners running rubric-based evaluation in CI.
offerings.job: Score repository responses against an AuraOne rubric and publish one consistent GitHub evidence surface.
offerings.differentiator: Annotations, job summary, outputs, threshold decision, and optional idempotent pull-request comment agree on one result.
offerings.proof: Action outputs, annotations, job summary, bot-owned comment, self-tests, and immutable-tag evidence.
offerings.boundary: Repository files are processed inside GitHub Actions; any model or hosted API access depends on the supplied judge configuration and secrets.
offerings.nextAction: Pin an immutable commit or verified release tag in a test repository and inspect permissions, outputs, and the generated evidence before enforcing a threshold.

offerings.audience: Data, model, and governance teams reviewing documentation in pull requests.
offerings.job: Validate required Datasheet, Model Card, and Data Card sections and surface actionable review findings.
offerings.differentiator: Blocking omissions and high-recall PII-like review signals are separated into one inspectable decision and one idempotent summary.
offerings.proof: Checked-file count, blocking failures, warnings, job summary, pull-request comment, and standalone validator report.
offerings.boundary: Markdown files are processed in CI; optional pull-request access uses the supplied GitHub token.
offerings.nextAction: Run advisory validation on representative cards, inspect false positives, and pin a verified immutable Action revision before blocking merges.

offerings.audience: Teams reviewing versioned evaluation rubrics in GitHub.
offerings.job: Diff and lint rubric changes, annotate affected lines, and publish one merge decision for the exact commit.
offerings.differentiator: The bot updates one Check Run and one marker-owned summary instead of producing duplicate or detached review noise.
offerings.proof: Rubric diff, lint findings, annotations, Check Run conclusion, summary marker, and deployed-app permission evidence.
offerings.boundary: The app reads configured rubric files and pull-request context and writes only approved Checks, annotations, and optional comments.
offerings.nextAction: Review app permissions and webhook events, test against a non-production repository, and verify deployed revision and rollback evidence.

offerings.offering: AuraOne Open catalog and developer documentation
offerings.audience: Engineers comparing AuraOne open-source tools and their release boundaries.
offerings.job: Explain every offering's job, audience, proof, boundary, install path, and release state without hiding blocked evidence.
offerings.differentiator: Source, registry, binary, capture, runtime, and support claims are shown as separate evidence classes.
offerings.proof: Canonical product pages, one selected flagship image per visual product, structured data, release records, and conversion events.

offerings.nextAction: Compare the exact source and release evidence for one offering before installing or downloading it.

offerings.audience: Evaluation engineers moving rubrics across frameworks.
offerings.job: Validate, lint, diff, and convert portable AuraOne Rubric Schema v1 files.

offerings.proof: Schema validation, lint findings, semantic diffs, adapter output, and conformance fixtures.
offerings.boundary: Rubric files are processed locally; adapters do not call a model unless a consuming workflow explicitly does so.
offerings.nextAction: Validate an existing rubric, inspect the normalized output, and pin the package version beside the rubric revision.

offerings.audience: Evaluation scientists and reviewer-quality teams.
offerings.job: Measure inter-annotator agreement with modern metrics, uncertainty, ordinal support, and missing-data handling.

offerings.proof: Metric output, confidence intervals, missing-data diagnostics, synthetic examples, and test vectors.
offerings.boundary: Annotation arrays are processed locally and no network access is required.
offerings.nextAction: Run the synthetic agreement examples, compare metrics for the same labels, and retain the package and input versions with the result.

offerings.audience: Teams relying on LLM judges for evaluation decisions.
offerings.job: Probe judge behavior for position, verbosity, self-preference, paraphrase, anchoring, and calibration failures.
offerings.differentiator: Synthetic diagnostic cases isolate judge failure modes before they are mixed into production evaluation scores.
offerings.proof: JSON and Markdown findings, plots, probe fixtures, calibration summaries, and reproducible run metadata.
offerings.boundary: Fixtures and reports remain local; model calls occur only through the judge provider configured by the operator.
offerings.nextAction: Run a small synthetic probe suite against the intended judge and record model, prompt, package, and result versions.

offerings.audience: Evaluation owners documenting an LLM judge before use.
offerings.job: Validate and render a disclosure record for judge prompts, calibration, bias, limitations, and intended use.
offerings.differentiator: The card keeps operational judge evidence beside the evaluation system instead of burying it in prose.
offerings.proof: Validated Judge Card JSON, rendered Markdown or HTML, calibration references, and known-limit records.
offerings.boundary: Card generation is local and does not invoke the documented judge.
offerings.nextAction: Generate a card for the current judge configuration and require it beside any evaluation result that depends on that judge.

offerings.audience: Evaluation platform engineers using multiple frameworks.

offerings.proof: Generated adapter files, normalized run configuration, fixtures, and round-trip or conformance checks.
offerings.boundary: Conversion is local; downstream framework network behavior is outside the adapter and must be reviewed separately.
offerings.nextAction: Convert a synthetic rubric for the intended framework and inspect the generated file before running any hosted evaluation.

offerings.audience: Framework and adapter maintainers claiming rubric-spec support.

offerings.proof: Conformance results, fixture-level failures, machine-readable output, and reproducible SVG badges.
offerings.boundary: Conformance runs locally against supplied adapter behavior and requires no hosted service.

offerings.audience: Evaluation and governance teams retaining reproducible run evidence.

offerings.nextAction: Generate a manifest for a synthetic run, verify every referenced digest, and retain it beside the release decision.

offerings.audience: Benchmark, evaluation, and dataset teams checking leakage risk.

offerings.proof: Finding records, matched spans or hashes, severity, configuration, summary report, and deterministic fixtures.

offerings.nextAction: Run against synthetic overlap cases first, inspect false positives, and retain the audit configuration beside the benchmark release.

offerings.audience: Teams reviewing prompts and rubrics through pull requests.

offerings.proof: Deterministic Markdown report, changed-file evidence, job summary, and idempotent pull-request comment.

offerings.audience: Reviewer-quality teams testing agreement and adjudication pipelines.

offerings.proof: Generated labels, seed and scenario metadata, expected disagreement properties, and reproducibility tests.

offerings.audience: Agent engineers and reviewers documenting individual runs or failures.
